text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your 17-year-old age, male gender, and the family history of bleeding, joint swelling, and easy bruising in an uncle, I need to ask: have you noticed bleeding into your joints (hemarthrosis) or muscle compartments in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A (Factor VIII deficiency).

The family history of bleeding and joint swelling in a male relative strongly suggests a sex-linked X-recessive disorder like Hemophilia A. Confirming this would require assessing specific coagulation factors.
